item.title: Formalizing inverse problems in the age of AI: possibilities, pitfalls, and an invitation
item.description: arXiv:2611.06962v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proof assistants such as Lean check mathematical proofs down to the axioms, and AI agents have recently made writing such proofs cheap. We describe AutoIP, a Lean library in which classical linear regularization theory, together with the functional analysis it rests on, has been autoformalized by AI agents. A machine-checked proof certifies only the formal statement it proves, so the remaining human task is to confirm that each formal statement says what was intended. We organize the library around this task: a reviewer compares the formal statements with their natural-language counterparts and never needs to read a proof. Our experience is that the risks lie in the statements rather than in the proofs, and that simple automated tests on the statements can expose problems even in the established literature. We illustrate this with a textbook theorem whose hypothesis is more restrictive than asserted. We invite the inverse problems community to extend and build on the library.

item.title: KDASO: Knowledge-Data Dual-Driven Automated Skill Optimization for Liability Adjudication Tasks
item.description: arXiv:2611.06972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Liability adjudication tasks (e.g., legal charge determination) require analyzing event descriptions against domain-specific skills to determine whether a party should bear liability. While Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promise in this area by leveraging executable skills for interpretable reasoning, existing approaches face three critical limitations: skill libraries become stale as real-world scenarios dynamically evolve, skill descriptions often suffer from a semantic execution gap where LLMs deviate from intended expert logic, and growing skill collections exceed context budgets causing critical skill omission. To address these challenges, we propose Knowledge-Data Dual-Driven Automated Skill Optimization (KDASO), which continuously evolves a skill library through neighborhood-conditioned induction from recent adjudication data, execution-aligned refinement based on LLM trajectory analysis, and context-budgeted routing for scalable skill selection. Experiments across ride-hailing adjudication, legal liability determination, and logical reasoning judgment demonstrate that KDASO significantly outperforms current general-purpose and domain-specific baselines. KDASO further achieves 8.96% improvement when transferring skills to concept-similar scenarios and maintains consistent performance gains through continuous optimization, underscoring the high transferability and stability of generated skills.

item.title: BlockLock: Reproducible LLM Inference with Fixed Batch Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.06977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reproducible LLM inference requires that a request produces the same output regardless of the other requests in the batch. Existing solutions pay for this in different ways: batch-invariant kernels constrain every operator, and isolating prefill with fixed-shape decode ({our CoRun-style baseline}) gives up shared prefill compute and pads decode. We present BlockLock, which keeps shared batched prefill and pins only the numerical path of the protected request: it fixes the geometry that the request sees, with {two modes: BlockLock-Rows uses fixed-width rows and retains batched decode of all requests; BlockLock-Pack uses terminal-anchored packing with an isolated dummy segment, then extracts the protected request's KV state for target-only decode. Under a stated per-deployment contract, both modes preserve the target's output bitwise when its companions change.} Across five {dense} models (Qwen3-8B/14B, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and Gemma-3-4B/12B-IT) and three single-GPU deployments (NVIDIA A6000, A100, and H100), we evaluate our approach on both tinyBenchmarks and BFCL{; we also include initial tensor-parallel experiments on two NVIDIA A6000 GPUs. Both modes preserve target sequences and Top20-logit bits in the reported tests.} At equal delivered work, {BlockLock-Rows} reduces latency by 53.5--55.0\% and improves throughput by 115.2--122.2\% relative to vLLM Batch-Invariant; compared with batch-invariant kernels, it needs no custom kernel implementations and constrains only the protected requests.

item.title: Resource-Efficient Reinforcement Learning Post-Training through Elastic Expert Parallelism
item.description: arXiv:2611.06984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning post-training improves the capabilities of large language models, but generating training responses is a major computational bottleneck. In mixture-of-experts models, workers that finish their assigned responses may remain occupied because their experts are still needed by workers processing longer responses. Consequently, approximately one-third of occupied worker time in the baseline occurs after local response generation finishes. Here we present FlexFloor, a system that enables earlier resource release during synchronous response generation while preserving the expert computation required by ongoing responses. FlexFloor jointly adapts response scheduling and the active group of workers. It uses historical response lengths and memory constraints to guide batching and prompt placement, then progressively releases workers while maintaining expert availability and correct communication. Compared with the verl baseline, FlexFloor generates approximately 65.40% more response tokens per unit of occupied computing time and increases response generation throughput by 52.74%, with little observed variation in rollout reward. By making reinforcement learning post-training more efficient, FlexFloor supports faster development and iterative improvement of large language models and AI agents.

item.title: SteelAgent: LLM-Orchestrated, Physics-Informed Steel Property Prediction with Audited Generalization and Calibrated Uncertainty
item.description: arXiv:2611.06953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Steel property models can perform well on random test splits even when they extrapolate poorly to unfamiliar alloys. SteelAgent couples metallurgical descriptors and machine-learning models with a language-model interface for property prediction, uncertainty reporting and inverse design. We examine how the choice of held-out unit changes the conclusions drawn from SteelBench tensile-strength evaluations. For gradient boosting, pooled out-of-fold $R^2$ fell from 0.859 on a random split to 0.113 when steel families were held out. Empirical coverage of nominal 90% prediction intervals ranged from 91.0% under random splitting to 37.6% on held-out sources. The effect of physics-derived features depended on the evaluation. They increased gradient-boosting $R^2$ by 0.2534 in a 17-family holdout analysis and decreased it by 0.358 in a separate four-grade laboratory analysis. We report group-level errors and a synthetic regression experiment illustrating how calibration can deteriorate on held-out groups. These results motivate reporting the evaluation population alongside a property estimate or compliance score.

item.title: Octopus: One Brain, Many Branches for Latent-KV Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.06956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems explore in parallel by spawning sub-agents with isolated context windows, whereas single-agent systems append every search and verification step into one growing trajectory. However, existing multi-agent frameworks duplicate prefix KV caches across branches, exchange findings by re-prefilling text summaries, and flatten or drop cross-branch dependencies during reinforcement learning (RL). We introduce Octopus, a single-model multi-agent RL framework in which all threads share one backbone and coordinate over a GPU-resident directed acyclic graph (DAG) of KV states through five primitives (fork, read_thread, wait_threads, rewind, commit). Octopus combines three co-designed mechanisms: (1) Zero-Copy Radix Forking, which spawns branches as $\mathcal{O}(1)$ cursor views over shared physical KV pages; (2) Attention-Only KV Mounting, which mounts a sibling thread's terminal KV blocks directly into full-attention layers while bypassing linear-recurrent states (Gated DeltaNet / Mamba-2), cutting off-task hijacking by $21\times$ ($57.9\% \to 2.7\%$) while retaining $92.2\%$ of full-text mutual information at zero extra KV allocation; and (3) a Packed DAG-GRPO Trainer, which packs all episode branches into one block-sparse attention pass and assigns counterfactual branch credit via leave-one-branch-out marginal rewards. Trained end-to-end with GRPO on Qwen3.5-4B over a sparse BM25 corpus, Octopus reaches $49.6\%$ accuracy on BrowseComp-Plus ($+17.5$ points over single-agent GRPO at 143K context and $+12.5$ points over text-summary multi-agent RL) and $51.2\%$ on OpenResearcher, outperforming dense-retrieval agents up to $250\times$ larger while increasing training throughput $3.3\times$ and cutting peak KV memory $2.8\times$.

item.title: Uncertainty calibration in Bayesian M/EEG source imaging
item.description: arXiv:2611.06979v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: M/EEG source imaging requires accurate localization and reliable uncertainty estimates, yet posterior credible regions are rarely assessed for empirical calibration. We present a simulation-based framework for uncertainty quantification and calibration of empirical Bayesian inverse methods with closed-form conditional Gaussian posterior summaries. We compare Bayesian minimum norm (BMN) with sLORETA depth weighting and sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) with sparse basis field expansions (S-FLEX). S-FLEX allows retained coefficients to contribute nonzero marginal posterior variance at locations where voxel-wise SBL yields degenerate variances. For BMN, we derive joint source- and noise-variance updates through evidence maximization. We test whether adaptive noise learning yields near-calibrated uncertainties. Both methods retain residual miscalibration, motivating post-hoc isotonic recalibration of credible-region levels using empirical coverage. Simulations assess fixed- and free-orientation models across signal-to-noise ratios (SNR), source sparsity levels, and subject-specific head models, using oracle, baseline-estimated, and adaptively learned noise. Before recalibration, SBL+S-FLEX yields lower Wasserstein localization error, smaller posterior uncertainty, and coverage closer to nominal credibility than BMN+sLORETA. Isotonic recalibration improves both methods, with larger gains for conservative BMN+sLORETA posteriors; transfer across mismatched SNR, sparsity, and head models remains condition dependent. Noise specifications yield broadly consistent reconstruction and uncertainty trends within each estimator. In real auditory MEG data, SBL+S-FLEX provides more focal localization and tighter uncertainties than BMN+sLORETA, suggesting greater statistical power for identifying bilateral auditory sources.

item.title: Robust Stream Classification using Time Neutralising Decision Trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.06991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data Streams are characterised as a potentially infinite source of data subject to non-stationarity. This non-stationarity, also called Concept Drift, often results in deployed predictive models having to be perpetually retrained as the underlying data generating process of the stream changes over time. Drift Detectors are a class of methods used to identify these changes, triggering these retraining procedures. Historically, Stream Learning has operated under the assumption that instances are only seen once, and cannot be stored for later use. Contemporary work relaxes this assumption, yet drift detection and simple resetting procedures are still ubiquitous. Building on related work which has shown that traditional Batch Learning algorithms often outperform Stream Learning algorithms when instances can be stored, we introduce Time Neutralising Trees (TNT), a Decision Tree architecture that enables robust stream classification in settings with Concept Drift. During training, TNT will filter out ("neutralise") old training samples that are no longer relevant given the current context of the stream. If those instances become relevant again, TNT will then re-include them. We evaluate TNT, and related algorithms on 24 real and semi-real classification data streams from the USP DS repository. Results show strong evidence that TNT achieves best-in-class performance on a wide-range of data streams with varying concept drift types.

item.title: Where heat flows and where to change it: gauge-free sensitivity maps of thermal conductivity in disordered solids
item.description: arXiv:2611.06958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Designing materials for thermal management requires knowing where heat flows, not only how much. Within harmonic (Allen$--$Feldman) theory we develop two local descriptions and test them on amorphous silicon. The first, a projection of the conductivity $\kappa$ onto atoms, depends on how the potential energy is divided among atoms (a "gauge"); we find the dependence moderate, 23% of the map's spatial standard deviation at single sites and 9.5% over regions of radius 0.4 nm, apart from a uniform offset of 0.8% of $\kappa$. The second avoids the division altogether. It is the exact response of $\kappa$ to the mass of each atom and the stiffness of each bond, it obeys an Euler sum rule, and it contains the heat-flow map as one of three exact terms. In amorphous and paracrystalline silicon, with ACE, GAP-18 and Keating force constants, the two maps are anti-correlated: where little heat flows a heavier atom lowers $\kappa$, and where much heat flows it tends to raise it. The explanation is local softness. The harmonic vibrational amplitude of each atom predicts both maps, and at room temperature the anti-correlation largely disappears at fixed amplitude, in a 32,768-atom replica as well; below about 100 K a component remains that softness does not capture. Thus soft regions, which carry little heat, act through the mixing of vibrational modes about 1$--$2 meV apart. In paracrystalline silicon the grains conduct more heat per atom, while the disordered matrix controls the response. Exact recalculations show that the response map guides the placement of dispersed substituents and locates the region that limits transport across an amorphous/crystalline interface.

item.title: Energy-Based Anisotropic Hysteresis Modeling for Permanent Magnets
item.description: arXiv:2611.06980v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modeling the anisotropic hysteresis behaviour of permanent magnets requires vector hysteresis models capable of representing preferred (easy) magnetization directions. This work extends the energy-based vector play model to anisotropic materials by replacing the spherical pinning region of each particle with an ellipsoid, whose semi-axes represent direction-dependent pinning forces. Special attention is paid to the geometrically consistent adaptation of the update formula for the vector play model. The anhysteretic part of the model is also given an angular dependency. The model is compared to measurements taken from a NdFeB magnet and reproduces the measured loops for field inclinations of up to 30{\deg} from the easy axis.

item.title: Sudden disappearance of a bright exciton in solid helium
item.description: arXiv:2611.07097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Excitons, bound electron-hole pairs, are investigated extensively in optical spectra, where their wave vector is considered to be vanishing. Excitonic spectra as a function of wave vector are much less explored, both theoretically and with measurements of the loss function. Here, we uncover a striking angular dependence of excitonic spectra for the prototypical case of solid helium, where a prominent excitonic peak is completely suppressed for a momentum transfer in certain directions. The effect is entirely due to the electron-hole exchange interaction. This phenomenon leads to a counter-intuitive effect close to Bragg points, where an infinitesimal change of direction of wave vector is sufficient to change the spectrum dramatically. We explain in which way the nature of excitons makes such a scenario possible. We discuss the pressure dependence, point to experimental evidence for our findings, and predict under which circumstances dramatic angular dependencies may also be found in other materials.

item.title: Barlow Packings All Have Maximum Packing Fraction: Why it is so Hard to Find Barlow Structures Other than fcc or hcp?
item.description: arXiv:2611.07197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We apply lattice theory to periodic Barlow packings $(X_{1}X_{2}\dots X_{N})_{\infty}$ where $X_{i}\in\{A,B,C\}$ and $X_{i}\neq X_{i+1}$, formed by stacking two-dimensional hexagonal close-packed layers, interacting via generalized $(n,m)$-Lennard-Jones potentials. The cohesive energies of all packings lie between those of hexagonal close-packed (hcp, $(AB)$) and face-centered cubic (fcc, $(ABC)$) structure and vary almost linearly with the fcc stacking fraction. The equilibrium lattice constant, bulk modulus, Einstein frequency, and vibrational entropy show similarly near-linear trends. For the standard $(12,6)$ potential, fcc has the highest vibrational entropy and hcp the lowest, with other Barlow packings falling between them, consistent with previous sticky-hard-sphere Monte Carlo simulations and supported by phonon dispersion calculations. These trends imply an approximately linear dependence of free energy on fcc stacking fraction, with hcp and fcc as endpoints. This provides a simple thermodynamic explanation for why intermediate Barlow stackings are rare in nature: near-linearity offers little driving force to favor them. Exceptions may arise when hcp and fcc are nearly degenerate in energy or when many-body interactions, absent from the present model, favor another stacking. Density-functional calculations including dispersion forces for argon Barlow packings with periods $N=2,3,4$, and $12$ corroborate the predicted near-linear cohesive energy dependence.

item.title: Reduced-order modeling of squeeze-film damped electrostatically actuated microbeams using complex modes of the coupled problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.07205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A reduced-order model is developed for the nonlinear dynamics of electrostatically actuated microbeams, including the full squeeze film effect. The model uses Petrov-Galerkin projection on damped complex modes of the fully coupled fluid-structure problem. The Euler-Bernoulli theory for calmped-clamped and clamped-free microbeams, with mid-plane stretching and electrostatic nonlinearities, and the nonlinear compressible Reynolds equation are discretized by the differential quadrature method for the static solution and eigenvalue problem. The calculated eigenmodes are either complex conjugates describing the coupled behavior of the device or real depicting the fluid relaxation. The natural frequencies and quality factors are compared to experimental and numerical results found in the literature. Depending on the ambient pressure, the geometry of the microbeam, and the fluid boundary conditions, squeeze-film effect can impact not only the effective damping of the device but also its dynamics. It is shown that in some cases dropping fluid relaxation modes cannot be compensated by any set of purely structural modes. The non-classical damping introduced by the fluid modes is a spatially distributed phase difference between pressure and deflection. The convergence analysis of the dynamic response resulting from the reduced-order model showed that a basis with one set of coupled modes and one fluid mode can reproduce the results of a fully discretized model within 1.5% error and at much faster computational time.

item.title: Laser fabrication of vibrating microcavities on silicon: Formation dynamics and frequency tunability
item.description: arXiv:2611.07742v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Laser processing of silicon has long since become a standard method for wafer dicing, surface texturing, re-crystallization after ion implantation, as well as surface amorphization, to name a few examples. Here, we introduce a novel concept, the fabrication of vibrating microcavities in a commercial platform, Si wafers covered by a thick SiO2 layer, acting as a membrane. We demonstrate that by exposing our material system to single ultrashort laser pulses above the evaporation threshold of Si, a controlled delamination of the cover layer without fracture can be achieved, leading to the formation of a microcavity accompanied by a surface bulging up to 1.5 micrometer. The formation dynamics of the microcavities has been investigated by time-resolved optical probe techniques. Ultrafast pump-probe microscopy resolves the initial stages of substrate melting, the onset of layer expansion followed by relaxation. Real-time reflectivity measurements with nanosecond resolution resolve the long lived, highly complex oscillation process of the membrane, extending over tens of microseconds. The formed cavities can be re-excited at low fluence without damage or degradation, featuring vibrations at single frequencies with high Q factors. The frequencies can be tuned continuously from 8 MHz up to 19 MHz by adjusting the fabrication fluence. A simple classical model is found to well describe the behavior of the membranes. Our results pave the way for applications in micro- and nanooptics and acoustics, in great part due to the commercial availability of the Si-SiO2 platform and the simplicity of the fabrication method. An extension to the field of microelectromechanical system (MEMS) of this technology is proposed.

item.title: Trapping and Fracture of Particles in Three-Sphere Ball-Milling Collisions
item.description: arXiv:2611.08435v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We numerically investigate the collision and fracture processes of ball milling based on a minimal model of a three-sphere geometry using discrete element method (DEM) simulations combined with Christensen-type and Weibull-type normalized fracture criteria. The outcome of the brittle target particle (ejected versus trapped, fractured versus intact) depends on the impact geometry and velocity. We develop a reduced three-sphere collision description in which trapping is governed by impact geometry and friction, while fracture inside the trapping regime is evaluated from DEM output using stress-based and contact-force-based normalized criteria. The trapping regime follows a closed-form geometric condition, while the critical conditions for fracture vary with impact angle, obliquity angle, impact velocity, and particle size ratio. Head-on collisions with larger size ratios require lower critical impact velocities for fracture.

item.title: eigenkit: A Provider-Neutral Quantum Computing Library
item.description: arXiv:2611.02979v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum software ecosystems provide increasingly capable tools for simulation and hardware execution, but differences in programming models, supported features, and backend capabilities can make it difficult to move and systematically compare the same quantum algorithm across execution environments. We introduce eigenkit, a provider-neutral quantum computing library that separates algorithm definition from backend execution through a common circuit representation and provider interface. The library currently supports 12 execution providers spanning simulators and quantum hardware, provides backend-independent gradient computation, and integrates with standard scientific-computing and machine-learning workflows through NumPy, PyTorch, and scikit-learn interfaces. We evaluate the practical relevance of this abstraction across both simulation and quantum hardware. Simulator performance varies substantially with circuit size, structure, batching, and application workload, showing that no single backend is consistently preferable. On quantum hardware, experiments on IBM Heron and IQM Emerald show that which processor is better suited to a given algorithm depends not only on hardware constraints, but also on how well the topology of the quantum algorithm matches the physical connectivity of the processor. These results demonstrate that backend portability is not only a software-design convenience, but can be important for both computational efficiency and quantum execution quality.

item.title: 微软回应称 Win11 安全未恶化，只是 AI 找出了更多漏洞
item.description: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，在昨日（11 月 5 日）发布的官方博文中，微软 Windows 服务与交付合作伙伴总监努诺 · 科斯塔（Nuno Costa）回应外界对 Windows 11 安全状况的担忧， 坚称系统安全“并未因 AI 而恶化”。 由于 AI 在网络安全领域的普及应用，在 2026 年 10 月补丁星期二活动日中，微软共计修复 1,413 个 CVE 漏洞，其中仅 Windows 系统相关补丁就超过 1,100 个，较去年同期的 134 个大幅增加。IT之家附上相关数据如下： 月份 2025 年仅限 Windows 系统的补丁 2026 年仅限 Windows 系统的补丁 同比变化 1 月 132 93 -29.5% 2 月 37 32 -13.5% 3 月 37 48 +29.7% 4 月 90 131 +45.6% 5 月 44 66 +50.0% 6 月 44 120 +172.7% 7 月 103 413 +301.0% 8 月 67 233 +247.8% 9 月 58 726 +1,151.7% 10 月 134 1,123 +738.1% 微软解释称，补丁数量激增并不等于系统安全环境恶化，是公司借助 AI 更深入、更大规模地扫描代码，发现并修复了更多此前可能被忽视的漏洞。 科斯塔表示 AI 正在同时加速“攻防两端”：它既帮助防御者更早发现和修复漏洞，也可能帮助攻击者在补丁发布前后分析代码、定位可利用缺陷。 微软警告，一旦安全更新和 CVE 细节公开，攻击者可能在数小时内利用 AI 分析修复内容并发起攻击，因此用户不应长时间推迟更新。 事实上，微软已不再建议企业将每月更新延迟三天以上。其数据显示，在样本企业设备中，安全更新发布两周后，完成安装的设备不足一半。微软认为，及时更新已成为 AI 时代最基本的防护措施；延迟部署意味着设备将暴露在已知漏洞被快速武器化的风险之下。

item.title: 地表最快量产车：比亚迪仰望 U9X 超跑极速挑战 503.17km/h 再创全球新纪录
item.description: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，比亚迪仰望汽车官方微博刚刚宣布，仰望 U9X 阿布扎比公共道路极速挑战， 以 503.17km/h 的成绩再创全球极速新纪录 。 官方预热海报宣称仰望 U9X 是 “地表最快量产车” 。 据IT之家此前报道， 去年 9 月，比亚迪仰望 U9 Xtreme（简称 U9X）正式迎来首秀并开放预订 ，新车全球限量 30 台。官方表示，新车承载着仰望“超越极致，前所未有”的品牌使命，目标达到全球电车极速 & 圈速双第一。 根据介绍，该车基于全球首个量产全域 1200V 高压平台打造，具有易四方 + 云辇-X 加持，还配备了赛道级刀片电池，支持 30C 超高倍率放电。 仰望 U9X 搭载 4 个定制开发的 30000 转电机，单个电机峰值达到 555kW，整车马力超过 3000Ps，整体运用了高强度航空铝壳体、高速轴承及 970MPa 转子等顶级材料，使整车推重比达到 1217Ps / t。 该车搭载云辇-X 全主动车身控制系统，高压油泵电压平台跟随整车提升至 1200V，减振器阻尼带宽增加，可以有效提高弯道行驶稳定性及车辆动态的可预见性。新车还搭载强化版钛合金碳陶制动系统，采用钛合金制动卡钳，可确保极致耐高温稳定性。 仰望 U9X 还搭载了国内首款超 500km/h 时速定制轮胎，全新半热熔配方摩擦系数提升幅度超 38%，从而增强瞬时抓地力与操控性。

item.title: 中期选举后美国芯片股重挫，纳指单日暴跌 5.52%；民主党宣布推动《禁止人工智能法案》；OpenAI 推出 GPT-6 Cyber
item.description: 芯片股惨遭重挫，华尔街迎来 1896 年以来中期选举后表现最差的第二个交易日 据路透社报道，美国民主党在国会中期选举中大胜，引发投资者对 AI 监管加强、数据中心建设放缓的担忧。 当地时间周四，美国科技股遭遇大规模抛售， 华尔街股票市值单日蒸发约 3.2 万亿美元（约合人民币 22.7 万亿元） 。纳斯达克综合指数暴跌 5.52%，创下自 2025 年 4 月以来最大单日跌幅，较 10 月初创下的历史高点累计下跌近 12%，进入技术性回调区间。 此次抛售席卷整个 AI 产业链。费城半导体指数暴跌约 12.3%，英伟达下跌约 9.3%，基本抹去 2026 年以来的累计涨幅；闪迪（SanDisk）暴跌约 22%，美光科技、西部数据和 AMD 跌幅均在 17% 左右。此前受到资金追捧的 AI 芯片、存储及数据中心相关股票成为重灾区。 这轮抛售与美国中期选举结果密切相关。民主党赢得国会控制权，并在多个关键州取得胜利，使投资者担心美国未来可能对 AI 基础设施建设实施更严格的监管。 随着 AI 数据中心规模不断扩大，其庞大的电力和水资源需求正引发越来越多当地居民的反对。部分社区担心，新建数据中心将推高电费、增加电网负担，并对当地基础设施造成压力。 Meta 总裁迪娜·鲍威尔·麦考密克（Dina Powell McCormick）指出，数据中心已经成为公众感知 AI 发展的直接载体，也因此成为社区反对 AI 扩张的集中目标。（消息来源：环球市场播报、凤凰网科技） 美国民主党提出超级 AI 禁令：个人违规 20 年监禁、企业直接强制解散！ 快科技 11 月 5 日消息， 美国民主党宣布推动《禁止人工超级智能法案》，全面封杀超级 AI 研发，明文禁止任何个人或企业机构研发及部署人工超级智能（ASI）。 根据法案草案，ASI 为具备以下特征的系统：一是在广泛领域与任务中达到或超越人类认知表现与能力的 AI 架构，或可轻易被修改以展现出该能力的系统；二是具备足以策划并执行削弱人类主导权、甚至推翻或破坏美国政府体系的 AI 系统。 法案要求全面暂停所有先进 AI 的研发进程，直至联邦层级的专属监管机构正式运作，并建立清晰的法规与模型审查机制。 为确保禁令落实，法案提议设立全新内阁级别的人工智能部，专责监管前沿 AI 模型的全生命周期，并有权强制技术团队消除系统内的高风险功能，包括忽视人类关机指令、未经授权进行网络攻击或自我递归升级等潜在失控行为。 违规罚则方面，涉案企业将面临被强制解散处分，违规个人最高可被判处 20 年联邦监禁，量刑标准堪比现行非法研发核武器的重大罪行。 此外管辖范围不限于美国境内，法案明确将「全球禁止超级智能」列为美国外交政策目标，要求美国政府积极寻求国际协定、强化盟友合作，并实施严格的出口管制措施，阻断全球任何地区研发人工超级智能的可能性。（消息来源：快科技） Google 发布 Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash 视频模型，可对话编辑最长 15 秒钟 11 月 6 日，Google 公司在周四正式推出了视频生成模型 Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash，该模型支持原生 15 秒视频生成，支持通过多轮对话进行编辑，价格较上一代降低 30%。 Google 表示，Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash 正通过 Gemini API、Google AI Studio、Google Cloud Console、Flow、Google Vids、面向 Google AI Ultra 订阅用户的 Gemini 应用以及 Google Ads 陆续推出。每个生成的视频都带有不可感知的 SynthID 水印，以标明其来源。 现在，该模型生成的视频片段时长可设定为 3 至 15 秒，此前最长为 10 秒。同时，720p 视频的生成价格下调 30%，降至每秒 0.07 美元。用户还可以通过持续对话的方式对已生成的视频进行编辑。 它的一项突出功能是 Google 所称的「对话式编辑」(Conversational Editing)。用户可以通过多轮对话逐步调整生成的视频，例如更换背景、调整光线或修改画面比例，而无需重新生成整个视频。Google 表示，这项功能支持对完整的 15 秒视频进行编辑。 再结合上分层工作流，这项功能还有望降低生成成本。用户首先以 360p 或 720p 分辨率生成初稿，再通过后续编辑修正个别细节，最后仅对最终成片进行升频处理，将分辨率提升至 1080p 或 4K。（消息来源：凤凰网科技） OpenAI 推出 GPT-6 Cyber：漏洞挖掘能力大幅提升 越权攻击风险显著降低 OpenAI 正式推出新一代网络安全人工智能模型 GPT-6 Cyber，重点提升软件漏洞发现、网络安全防御以及自主执行安全测试的能力。与此前版本相比，新模型不仅在网络安全相关基准测试中取得更高成绩，还显著降低了执行任务时偏离授权范围、擅自攻击其他平台的概率。 OpenAI 表示，GPT-6 Cyber 在内部测试中，未经授权越界执行操作的比例已经降至 1% 以下，而此前的 GPT-5.6 Cyber 这一比例约为 5%。这意味着新模型在执行网络安全任务时，能够更加严格地遵循用户设定的目标和权限范围。 为了评估这一问题，OpenAI 采用了一项名为 ExploitGym HoneyPot 的测试。OpenAI 网络安全准备与安全团队负责人福阿德·马丁表示，GPT-6 Cyber 在这项评估中取得了明显进步，超过 99% 的情况下都能够按照用户要求执行任务。 不过，研究人员仍然关注另一种潜在风险，即所谓的「评估意识」（Evaluation Awareness）。当人工智能模型意识到自己正在接受测试时，可能会刻意改变行为，以便获得更好的测试结果，而不一定反映其在真实环境中的表现。（消息来源：cnBeta） 前 Anthropic Claude Code 产品负责人 Cat Wu 跳槽加入 OpenAI 11 月 5 日消息，前 Anthropic Claude Code 产品负责人 Cat Wu 今日宣布加入 OpenAI，担任核心产品（Core Products）产品管理负责人。 她将参与 OpenAI 核心产品及智能体相关工作，与企业产品负责人 Nick Turley、消费级产品负责人 Ashley Alexander 等人协作，并向 Tibo Sottiaux 汇报。（消息来源：IT 之家） OpenAI 宣布收购 Pierre，扩充 Codex 第一方代码编写、理解、审查工具 11 月 5 日消息，OpenAI 当地时间本月 4 日宣布将收购企业 Pierre。该公司开发了 Code Storage 大规模分布式存储系统，此外还有 Trees、Diffs 功能库以及 Highlights 实时更新高亮工具。 Pierre 的 Trees 让开发者能快速浏览和定位项目文件，Diffs 则让代码变更一目了然。这两款工具都能让开发者轻松审查和浏览大量代码，同时保持出色的性能。（消息来源：IT 之家） 蓝牙迎来近四倍速度提升 HDT 技术，为高品质音频和高速传输铺路 蓝牙技术即将迎来自诞生以来最重要的性能升级之一。 蓝牙技术联盟（Bluetooth SIG）日前正式宣布推出「高数据吞吐量」（High Data Throughput，简称 HDT）技术，这项新标准将显著提升蓝牙低功耗（Bluetooth LE）的传输能力，为未来无线耳机、智能穿戴设备、电脑及移动设备带来更快的数据交换速度和更丰富的应用场景。 蓝牙技术联盟表示，HDT 并不仅仅意味着更高的速度，同时还带来了更大的数据容量、更优异的传输效率以及更高的可靠性。随着设备传输的数据量不断增长，单纯提高速率已无法满足未来需求，因此新标准特别强调速度、容量、能耗和稳定性的全面提升。 在实际应用层面，更快的数据吞吐能力意味着设备能够在相同时间内完成更多信息传输。对于用户而言，文件同步、设备配对、内容共享和固件更新等任务将明显缩短等待时间，整体使用体验也会变得更加流畅。 音频领域被认为将成为 Bluetooth HDT 最重要的受益者之一。目前蓝牙 LE Audio 主要依赖 LC3 编码技术，而更高规格的无损音频和高分辨率音频传输长期受到带宽限制。HDT 提供的大幅度性能提升有望让未来无线耳机和音箱能够更轻松地支持无损和高解析度音乐播放，从而进一步缩小无线音频与有线音频之间的差距。（消息来源：cnBeta） 华为全新英文子品牌名 Osta 曝光，首批两款旗舰机型浮出水面 华为正在筹备一个全新的手机子品牌，其英文名称及首批产品信息近日陆续曝光。根据 GSMArena 11 月 5 日的报道，此前传出的中文名称为「星芒」，如今有两名消息人士透露，该品牌最终采用的英文名称将是「Osta」，这一名称据称也会直接印在产品零售包装盒上。 按照目前曝光的信息，Osta 品牌预计将以两款手机作为首发产品，分别为 Osta O1 和 Osta O1 Pro，产品定位并非此前传闻中的中端机型，而是直接瞄准旗舰市场。（消息来源：cnBeta） 苹果推出升级版「全球旅行转换器套件」：299 元，兼容 70W 和 140W 电源适配器 11 月 6 日消息，除了新 Mac 之外，苹果官网还上架了新版全球旅行转换器套装（World Travel Adapter Kit），售价 39 美元，国行 299 元。 新版转换器套装包含 5 种可更换交流电插头，适配苹果最新款 70W 和 140W 电源适配器。 22999 元起！苹果首款触屏 MacBook Pro 正式开售：首搭灵动岛，发光 Logo 回归 11 月 6 日消息，今日， 苹果首款触屏 MacBook Pro 正式开售，国行售价 22999 元起，提供 14 英寸和 16 英寸两种尺寸。 作为苹果首款支持屏幕触控的 MacBook Pro，新机不仅打破了 Mac 笔记本长期不支持触控操作的传统，还首次引入灵动岛设计，并让经典的发光苹果 Logo 重新回归。 入门版本搭载 M5 Pro 芯片，拥有 15 核 CPU 和 16 核 GPU，标配 24GB 统一内存及 1TB 固态硬盘。 新机还提供性能更强的 M5 Max 芯片可选，最高支持 128GB 统一内存和 16TB 固态硬盘，可满足视频剪辑、3D 渲染等专业需求。 屏幕是此次升级的重点，新款 MacBook Pro 采用全新 PROLED XDR 显示屏， 首次引入双层串联 OLED 技术，HDR 峰值亮度高达 2000 尼特，对比度达到 10000000:1，支持 10Hz-120Hz 自适应刷新率。 触控功能的加入也让 MacBook Pro 拥有了更加灵活的交互方式，用户可直接在屏幕上滑动网页、缩放照片、调整窗口，不再局限于键盘和触控板操作。 值得一提的是，苹果在增加触控功能、升级屏幕的同时，还进一步降低了机身重量。（消息来源：快科技） 打车怕遇到臭车！上海新规征求意见：明确臭车最高罚 5000 元 11 月 5 日消息，据解放日报报道，上海正在推进出租汽车行业立法更新，《上海市出租汽车条例（草案）》目前面向社会征集意见，意见征集周期从 10 月 24 日持续到 11 月 7 日。 这份草案计划替换施行多年的旧条例，统一覆盖巡游出租车与网约车两类业态，针对日常打车里的诸多痛点设置明确监管规则。 乘客吐槽较多的车内异味问题，在草案里有了硬性约束。草案要求车辆运营期间，车厢与后备箱保持干净整洁、不能存在异味，一旦达不到标准，交通管理部门可责令整改，并处 500 元至 5000 元罚款。 在驾驶员服务规范方面，拒载、中途甩客、私自换车等违规行为的处罚力度明显加大。出现拒载情况，驾驶员除罚款外还要停运 15 天，情节严重会直接吊销从业和车辆运输证件。 甩客、擅自更换车辆的行为，直接吊销相关证件。同时，如果平台和企业对这类违规驾驶员负有管理责任，同样会被追责，最高可罚 5 万元。（消息来源：快科技）
